ledger.claim: Corroboration beyond the trace exists in any event, and POL-RD-08 obliges the rider to supply it: the rider's own counters are deviation_claims_60d 5 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 1 on EV-RPROF-00107, and this claim's excess is 25.5%, under 30%, so POL-RD-08's fourth sentence applies. It is satisfied from outside the trace. The driver's own counterparty_statement admits the route taken: 'I went by Newton and Kim Seng to avoid it.' And EV-CHAT-00107 shows the rider putting the Whitley exit to him - 'why exit at whitley? CTE goes straight down what' - with the driver not denying the exit but answering 'cte very jam tonight boss'. POL-RD-07(ii) names a counterparty statement admitting the route as exactly this class of independent corroboration, and POL-RD-08 says the factor may never be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven.

The driver's explanation does not exonerate him. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory that names a road, expressway segment or junction the optimal route traverses and carries a validity window overlapping the time the trace would reach that segment. There is no such artifact: EV-ADVIS-00107-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, with a BLOCKING MISSING_ARTIFACT issue - no congestion advisory was issued for the CTE on the evening of 18 July 2026. The driver's 'CTE very jam tonight boss' names no artifact and no road segment, and POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden once the rider has shown the excess. With nothing to exonerate, POL-RD-03's cap never runs and no part of the 3.57 km excess is set aside.

The driver cannot fall back on a rider-requested detour. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction in the chat log that identifies a place or road specifically enough to act on, corroborated by a waypoint_hint the vehicle passes within 200 m of. EV-CHAT-00107 contains exactly one rider message and it is a challenge to the detour, not a request for one, and both messages carry waypoint_hint null. On the clause's own terms the corroboration test is undecidable, the clause is unavailable, and the ruling must record that the test could not be run.

The refund is then arithmetic, not discretionary. EV-FARE-00107 shows fare_model METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs and the upfront-fare clause POL-RD-11 has no application. Surge lives on the fare breakdown and nowhere else - EV-FARE-00107 carries surge_multiplier 1.35 - so recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 14.00 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.35) + 0.80 platform fee = 29.177, with no ERP, tolls, surcharge or waiting-time fee to add. The rider was charged 36.60 (EV-FARE-00107, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0). Refund = 36.60 - 29.177 = 7.423, which is not rounded at any intermediate step and is rounded up at the end to SGD 7.45. That is 20.3% of charged_total - above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so not NO_ACTION, and far below the 90% that would make it a FULL_REFUND under POL-RD-06(b) or POL-RD-02's closing sentence. The outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 7.45 and the ruling should state charged_total, recomputed_fare and the refund on separate lines.

No pass-through correction is added on top of that figure, and none is double-counted. EV-FARE-00107 records erp_gantries: [] and a tolls_erp of 0.0, with an off-optimal-route ERP total of 0.00 and no airport surcharge line on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. POL-RD-09 therefore has nothing to refund and nothing to add, and the rider does not ask for a line the fare breakdown does not carry. The SGD 7.45 above is the whole of the rider's recovery.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. Trip TRP-00107, 18 July 2026, Ang Mo Kio to Raffles Place. The deviation is ESTABLISHED. POL-RD-01 measures the actual distance on the GPS trace and the optimal on the trip record. EV-GPS-00107 gives a trace distance of 17.57 km; EV-TRIP-00107 gives an optimal of 14.00 km. The excess is 3.57 km, 25.5% of optimal. That clears both establishment gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so a deviation exists. It is below both materiality gates (8.0 km and 50%), so this is an ordinary deviation and POL-RD-06's uplift to a full refund does not apply. The GPS trace and the confidence cap. EV-GPS-00107 is IMPAIRED at the admissibility layer — weight 0.30, issue codes GPS_DRIFT and IMPLAUSIBLE_SPEED (a 331.8 m multipath outlier on the Raffles Place final approach) — but it is NOT impaired for policy under POL-RD-07: no gap over 90 s (max gap 0.0 s), no jump over 500 m, no sustained sampling interval over 30 s. I say both things, as the clause requires. The 0.30 weight bears on confidence only. The finding survives that discount: the route is carried independently by the chat log EV-CHAT-00107 (weight 1.0), which records the rider putting the Whitley exit to the driver and the driver not denying it, and by the driver's own counterparty statement ("I went by Newton and Kim Seng"). Under POL-GEN-02(2) the cap is the higher of the independent carriers — 1.0 — not the 0.30 of the down-weighted trace alone; bundle_integrity_score is context and is not the cap. The driver's traffic excuse does not exonerate him. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic advisory naming the affected corridor with an overlapping validity window. There is none: EV-ADVIS-00107-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) — no congestion advisory was issued for the CTE that evening. "CTE very jam tonight boss" is a general assertion unsupported by any advisory ID; under POL-RD-08 it does not discharge the driver's burden and sets aside no part of the excess. POL-RD-04 does not apply either: the only rider message challenges the detour rather than requesting one, and both messages carry waypoint_hint null, so the clause's corroboration test could not be run. The refund. EV-FARE-00107 shows fare_model METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs and the upfront-fare clause POL-RD-11 has no application. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 × 14.00 + 0.28 × 24.0) × 1.35) + 0.80 = 29.177, using the surge_multiplier 1.35 read from the fare breakdown. Charged_total = 36.60. Refund = 36.60 − 29.177 = 7.423, rounded up to SGD 7.45. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% full-refund share. POL-RD-09 adds nothing: the fare carries no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge, so the 7.45 is the whole of the recovery and no pass-through correction is double-counted. No driver compensation is due, the billed distance not being less than the trace. Profile. POL-RD-06's repeat-deviation check is not met — deviation_flags_90d 1 against completed_trips_90d 619 — so there is no conduct referral. The high lifetime counters on the rider's profile (lifetime_trips, prior_disputes_filed, prior_disputes_upheld, prior_no_show_flags, rating, cancellation_rate) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and no finding rests on them. Ruling: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 7.45; the charge of SGD 36.60 stands less that refund.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
